question: Which ATT&CK techniques does CAPEC-21 (Exploitation of Trusted Identifiers) map to, and what mitigations apply to those techniques?

answer.headline: Gathered 4 record(s) from 2 source(s); 3 cross-source correlation(s) on shared identifiers.
answer.narrative: CAPEC-21 (Exploitation of Trusted Identifiers) maps to the ATT&CK techniques T1134 (Access Token Manipulation), T1528 (Steal Application Access Token), and T1539 (Steal Web Session Cookie). Mitigations for T1539 include Update Software (M1051), Audit (M1047), Software Configuration (M1054), Multi-factor Authentication (M1032), User Training (M1017), and Restrict Web-Based Content (M1021). T1528 is mitigated by Audit (M1047), User Account Management (M1018), User Training (M1017), and Restrict Web-Based Content (M1021), while T1134 is addressed by Privileged Account Management (M1026) and User Account Management (M1018).

records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: An adversary guesses, obtains, or "rides" a trusted identifier (e.g. session ID, resource ID, cookie, etc.) to perform authorized actions under the guise of an authenticated user or service.
